title: Recapitulation
hookLine: Irenaeus: Christ lives every stage of human life again, rightly, to heal it

lines: A BABY, A BOY, A CARPENTER.
THE STAGES ARE PART OF THE RESCUE.
cards: A baby who has to be fed. A boy who stays behind in the city and leaves his parents searching. A man the neighbors know as the carpenter.
A grown man with friends, enemies, and a job to finish. That's Jesus, and also the stages a human life can pass through.
Luke pauses on the in-between years with one line: "And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man." He grew. He didn't arrive finished.
An early bishop named Irenaeus thought those ordinary stages weren't a detour on the way to the cross. They were part of the rescue.

teach.h: GOING OVER IT AGAIN, FROM THE TOP.
teach.b: Recapitulation means going over it again, from the top. Irenaeus was a bishop in Gaul, in what is now France, and he found the idea in a line in Ephesians: God's plan is to "gather together in one all things in Christ."
The human story went wrong at its head, with Adam. So Christ comes as a new head and lives the story over again, this time rightly.

teach.h: IN ADAM ALL DIE, IN CHRIST ALL ALIVE.
teach.b: Paul puts the two side by side: "For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive."
And to the Romans: "For as by one man's disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous." Irenaeus loved the matching details.

teach.h: A TREE, A KNOT, A YES.
teach.b: A disobedience at a tree in the garden; an obedience on a tree outside Jerusalem. Eve tied a knot by her disobedience; he pictured Mary untying it by her obedience, her yes. And he went through the ages of life.
Christ became an infant, he wrote, to make infants holy; a child for children; a young man for the young.
Each stage, in his telling, Christ passed through and lived whole. So the cross isn't the only place where saving happens. The manger is too.
The workbench is too. The hungry days in the desert are too. The cross and the empty tomb finish it.
Like a song played again from the top: the same tune, but this time every note true.

how: Christians who follow the church year walk through Christ's life each year, from his birth at Christmas through his childhood, ministry, death and resurrection, and Irenaeus is honored as a saint in Catholic and Orthodox churches.

games.why: recapitulation: Christ as a new head, living every stage over again, so the story is healed from the inside.

practice: Name the stage of life you're in right now: starting out, in the thick of it, raising someone, caring for someone, slowing down, starting over. Ask what it's asking of you, patience, courage, letting go, and stay with the answer.
If you pray, pray for this stage as one Christ has walked; if you don't, just let it be seen, all of it.
